Does anyone here know anything about the patent system? I'm trying to file a patent and the lawyer wants $15,000 to do it. There's got to be a cheaper way to do it.

I studied patent law in law school. I am not a patent attorney, however. $15k is pretty much the going rate for a patent attorney to file a patent.

Theoretically, you can try to file the patent yourself, but you are highly unlikely to ever get your patent granted unless it is some completely new area of creation in which there is no previous known work.
Thanks for the advice, is there any type of protection of you pay the $15,000 and the patent doesn't go through?

If you mean like a refund, then no.

However, that is kind of the point of hiring the patent attorney in the first place. The attorney should conduct a diligent search for previous known inventions. Once that is complete, the attorney should be able to tell you if you have a good chance at getting your patent granted. There are no guarantees unfortunately. In fact, the patent being granted the first time it is submitted is likely to be denied because that's just how the United States Patent Office works. They usually want something refined or better described. It is kind of a back and forth process until the patent agent gets a better understanding of what you are trying to patent.

It is kind of funny because obviously you know your invention inside and out. However, when you see the patent application, should you use an attorney to write it, you will likely not have any idea what the heck the application is talking about. Patent language is akin to a foreign language all its own. A mix of engineering parlance and legalese.
It's almost like they designed this system to discourage the independent inventors.
